idle: The sky is the work. The ground still keeps old tools if you look.
A rock is a rock until you have something to compare it with.
wren.missionNudge: The solar marker is east of the dome. Start there before you chase the crater.
wren.afterComplete: The campaign window is written. The desert will still be here after dark.

items.name: Dark heavy rock
items.text: Dark, heavier than the pale stones around it, a dull rind. It is a rock until you have a comparison.
items.interpretedText: The drawer sample matches: dense, dark, a fused rind. A meteorite fragment, earned by comparison, not by guessing the crater.
items.wrenHint: There is a dark stone on the crater floor. Do not name it from a story.
items.wrenAck: Heavy and dark is observation. Meteorite is interpretation. They are not the same sentence.

items.name: Old sundial
items.text: A sundial with a cracked face. Someone trusted this shadow before the notebooks started arguing.
items.wrenHint: East of the dome there is an older way of asking the Sun what time it is.
items.wrenAck: A sundial is a gnomon with manners.

items.name: Solar-weathered marker
items.text: A stake whose paint has gone pale on the south face and held color on the north. Light has a direction here.
items.wrenHint: On the way to the mesa a stake has been cooked by the Sun on one side only.
items.wrenAck: South face fades first. That is a year of light, not a week of wind.

items.name: Desert varnish
items.text: The outcrop wears a dark film on the exposed face. The underside, where you can reach, is paler.
items.wrenHint: The west outcrop is stained. Look at which face takes the sky.
items.wrenAck: A coating is not the rock. Same rule as a shadow is not the Sun.

items.name: Crater rim
items.text: Broken rock on a raised ring around a low basin. From here the eastern sky sits later than it does on the mesa.
items.wrenHint: Walk the east ring. Notice what the wall does to sunrise.
items.wrenAck: A wall can hide a rising Sun. That matters if you pick a site at night.

items.name: Historic survey post
items.prompt: A brass cap in the dust.
items.text: Latitude is stamped on the post. The tablet should agree if you stand close.
items.wrenHint: There is an older survey post east of the dome. Coordinates still work in a desert.
items.wrenAck: The number on the post is a pair, not a decoration.

items.name: Telescope foundation
items.text: A concrete ring and empty bolts. Whatever sat here was aimed at sky, not at the wash.
items.wrenHint: Behind the dome the pad is still there. The instrument is not.
items.wrenAck: A foundation remembers a pointing even when the tube is gone.

items.name: Alignment stones
items.text: Three stones. The line points at the mesa rim, not at the dome. Someone cared where the sky met the land.
items.wrenHint: South of the wash, stones in a short line. See where they aim.
items.wrenAck: A line on the ground can be a horizon note.

items.name: Night-sky viewpoint
items.text: From the rim the desert is a dark plate and the sky is the rest of the world. This is where Moon notes belong.
items.wrenHint: The mesa rim is the dark site. Station lights stay in the basin.
items.wrenAck: Night is not a theme. It is a working condition.
